fix(datastore): treat a missing dynamic threshold as a successful delete on v2

## Description

Resetting a species' dynamic threshold on a v2 database left the species stuck in the pending reset queue. The reset deletes the stored row and queues the species so the persistence tick can delete anything left over. On v2 the delete returned a "dynamic threshold not found" error when no row matched, and the tick requeues a species on any error. So every single-species reset logged two warnings and requeued the species every 30 seconds until restart. If the species was learned again, the next tick also deleted its fresh row and its threshold events once.

`v2only.Datastore.DeleteDynamicThreshold` now treats a missing row as a successful delete, like the legacy store does. Any other error is still returned, so a real database failure is still logged and requeued.

What changes for users: after a reset, no repeated warnings and no requeueing; a species learned again after the first tick keeps its row and events. The only caller change is the reset path and the persistence tick, both of which already handle a nil result as "nothing left to delete".

None.

fix(claude): ask Git about local settings from their own folder

## Outcome

The five adapter test groups from #2760 that failed on Windows pass there, and Claude Code auto memory keeps loading the personal memory index on Windows when `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` is on. This is the second of the #2760 slices.

## Root cause

A Windows diagnostic run (https://github.com/Chemaclass/agnostic-ai/actions/runs/40847675509) showed three causes, not the single path mismatch the issue guessed:

1. Short and long names. The runner's temp folder is `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...`, while `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` answers `C:/Users/runneradmin/...`. `repositorySuppliedLocalSettings` in `internal/adapters/claude/auto_memory.go` took the settings path relative to that top level, got `..\..\..\..\..\..\RUNNER~1\...`, and `git ls-files` exited 128. The error counted as "repository supplied", so untracked local settings were blocked. A linked project folder (macOS `/var`) hit the same bug. This is a product bug: it now asks Git from the settings file's own folder, with a path relative to that folder, so both sides share one spelling.
2. Skills folder keys. `emit.Session.SetSkillsDirWriters` stored the caller's keys as given, while `SkillsDirWrittenByOthers` looks up `filepath.Clean(dir)`. The production caller already cleaned its keys, so only callers with slash keys (the Crush test) missed on Windows. The session now cleans the keys it stores, and the Copilot test drops its own `filepath.Clean`.
3. Test lookups with the wrong separator. The CLI and the dry-run preview print native paths on purpose (`import_preview.go` uses `filepath.FromSlash`, and its tests expect it). The `TestAgentMCP_*`, OpenCode dry-run, Ellipsis parity, and Ellipsis import dry-run tests looked for slash paths, so they now look for the native form.

## Validation

- Windows, named packages: https://github.com/Chemaclass/agnostic-ai/actions/runs/40853970824 ran `go test -race ./internal/adapters/...` on this branch. `internal/adapters`, `claude`, `crush`, `ellipsis`, `opencode`, `copilot`, and `internal/emit` pass; the only failure is the Gemini test that #2768 fixes. https://github.com/Chemaclass/agnostic-ai/actions/runs/40854510826 ran the two Ellipsis import dry-run tests in `internal/cli` and passed. Both runs used a temporary branch that changed only the Windows test step; it is deleted.
- Windows, full dispatch on this branch: https://github.com/Chemaclass/agnostic-ai/actions/runs/40853944452. Every package before the 10-minute cut passes except `internal/adapters/gemini` (#2768); `internal/cli` is cut by the limit, which a later slice raises.
- Local (macOS): the new `TestAutoMemoryLoadsPersonalIndex_PermissionsFollowGitUnderAnotherRootSpelling` and `TestSkillsDirWrittenByOthers_MatchesAnySpellingOfTheFolder` failed before the fix and pass after it. `go test -count=1` passes for `internal/adapters`, `claude`, `crush`, `ellipsis`, `opencode`, `copilot`, and `internal/emit`, plus the two Ellipsis import dry-run tests in `internal/cli`. `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, and `GOOS=windows go vet` on `./internal/adapters/...` and `./internal/cli` pass. `make size-check`: 24133792 bytes, 8192 under the budget.
- The full local gate (`make ci-local`) is pending and runs separately before merge.

## Not in this pull request

- #2769: a tracked `.claude/Settings.Local.json` in another letter case reads as untracked. This predates the change.
- The `internal/cli`, `tests/integration`, and `scripts/audit-manifest` failures listed in the issue comment go in a separate slice.

Related to #2760

Ignore what pg_get_viewdef adds to a function in FROM

`pg_get_viewdef` rewrites a function in `FROM` when it prints a view:

- It writes `LATERAL` on a function whose arguments read an earlier FROM item, and keeps a `LATERAL` that was written on one that reads none.
- It writes out the column that a one-column function gets from a table alias, so `unnest(x) t` comes back as `unnest(x) t(t)`.

Because of this, a view written as `FROM t, unnest(t.tags) AS u(tag)` or `FROM generate_series(1, 3) AS g` was replaced on every `plan`.

On a function, `LATERAL` is a noise word, because the arguments can read earlier FROM items either way. `equalViewDef` now drops it from `RangeFunction` on both sides before it compares the definitions. A sub-query keeps its `LATERAL`, because there it decides which relation a name resolves to. A column alias that holds only the table alias's name is dropped on both sides as well.

Not covered:

- A composite-returning function with no column list, such as `jsonb_each(x) j`, which is stored as `j(key, value)`.
- `WITH ORDINALITY t` with no column list.

`pista dump` output already planned clean before this change and still does.

## Tests

- `TestEqualViewDef_fromFunctionLateral` and `TestEqualViewDef_fromFunctionColumnAlias` in `diff/views_test.go`. Each also checks cases that must still compare unequal: a sub-query with and without `LATERAL`, a column alias with a different name, and changed function arguments.
- `testdata/plan/no_diff_view_from_function.yml`: five common forms plan clean.
- `testdata/plan/modify_view_from_function.yml`: a change to the function's arguments still produces `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`.

I ran `make test` locally on PostgreSQL 16. Everything passed except `TestPlan_WithPassword`, which fails on main too because of password authentication on the local server. `golangci-lint run` reported 0 issues.

test(gemini): drive only the command writers in the namespaced agent test

## Outcome

`TestEmit_NamespacedAgentCommandSharesTheCommandPath` passes on Windows. This is the first of three slices for #2760.

## Root cause

The test emitted an agent named `vc:save` through the whole Gemini adapter. Before the command writers run, the adapter writes the agent's own subagent file, `.gemini/agents/vc:save.md`. Windows stores a colon name as a hidden stream, so the emit session refuses that write, and the test failed with `refusing to write a name with a colon ... .gemini\agents\vc:save.md`. The check it makes, that the command owns `.gemini/commands/vc/save.toml` and no colon file is written, never ran.

That refusal is the documented rule for a target that writes the name as one file (`docs/site/content/docs/configuration.md#path-semantics`). Gemini CLI reads subagents only from the flat `.gemini/agents/*.md` folder, so mapping the colon to a folder there would hide the agent. The production code stays as it is.

## Change

- The test calls `emitAgentCommands` and then `emitCommands`, the two command writers, so it checks the command path the same way on every system. `TestEmit_Agent_AndCommand_SameNameNoLongerCollide` still covers the order inside `Emit`.
- The Gemini target page says an agent keeps its name as one file, so Windows sync refuses an agent named with a colon, and links the path rules.

## Validation

- Windows: dispatch run https://github.com/Chemaclass/agnostic-ai/actions/runs/40847299828 (`full_windows=true`) on 691a99e5; the later commit changes only the docs and a test comment. The job "Test (windows-latest)" still ends red and is cancelled at its 10-minute limit, which slices 2 and 3 of #2760 address. In that run `internal/adapters/gemini` passes (`ok ... internal/adapters/gemini 2.189s`); it failed in run 40845206340 before this change.
- Local (macOS): `go test -count=1 ./internal/adapters/gemini/ -run 'TestEmit_Namespaced|SameName'`, `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, and `GOOS=windows go vet` pass. `make size-check`: 24133792 bytes, 0 under the budget.

fix(ci): use install_steps hook

## What?

Migrate `homebrew_casks.hooks.post.install` to the declarative `install_steps` DSL in `.goreleaser.yml`.

```yaml
hooks:
  post:
-   install: |
-     if OS.mac?
-       system_command "/usr/bin/xattr", args: ["-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", "#{staged_path}/matcha"]
-     end
+   install_steps: |
+     run "/usr/bin/xattr", args: ["-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", "{{ .StagedPath }}/matcha"]
```

The `if OS.mac?` guard is dropped because a cask only installs on macOS. Behavior is unchanged: the Apple quarantine xattr is still stripped from the binary after install.

## Why?

`goreleaser` v2.19 deprecated the arbitrary-Ruby `hooks.post.install` hook in favor of `install_steps`, and `goreleaser check` **fails with exit code 2** when a config uses deprecated properties:

```
• DEPRECATED:  homebrew_casks.hooks.post.install  should not be used anymore,
  check https://goreleaser.com/deprecations#homebrew_caskshookspostinstall
• .goreleaser.yml  error=configuration is valid, but uses deprecated properties
⨯ check failed     error=1 out of 1 configuration file(s) have issues
```

The `goreleaser` job in `ci.yml` installs the action's **latest** release (`install-only: true`, no pinned version), so this started failing without any change on our side. It currently breaks the `goreleaser` check on `master` (run [40280225715](https://github.com/floatpane/matcha/actions/runs/40280225715) at 87b6274) and on every open PR.

## Verification

With goreleaser **v2.19.0** (the version CI resolves to):

```
$ goreleaser check -f .goreleaser.yml
  • 1 configuration file(s) validated
  • thanks for using GoReleaser!          # exit 0

$ goreleaser check -f .goreleaser.nightly.yml
  • 1 configuration file(s) validated     # exit 0
```

Checking the previous config reproduces the CI failure exactly:

```
$ goreleaser check -f <old .goreleaser.yml>
  • DEPRECATED:  homebrew_casks.hooks.post.install ...
  ⨯ check failed     error=1 out of 1 configuration file(s) have issues   # exit 2
```

benchmarks.task_description:
Look up the shared mode Service CIDR from the default ServiceCIDR

Read the shared mode Service CIDR from the default `kubernetes` ServiceCIDR object, falling back to the current lookups on older hosts.

On 1.33+ the failing Service no longer returns the valid range, so `status.serviceCIDR` was always empty and K3s used its `10.43.0.0/16` default, which breaks the Service sync on hosts with a different range, like EKS.

Added unit tests for the lookup, a status check in the integration tests, and an assertion in the Service sync e2e spec that the virtual cluster uses the host Service CIDR. That last one fails on main on K3s too, since the status is empty there as well.

Ref #1355

diff --git a/pkg/controller/cluster/cluster.go b/pkg/controller/cluster/cluster.go
index 6391eec2..f2bcdae4 100644
--- a/pkg/controller/cluster/cluster.go
+++ b/pkg/controller/cluster/cluster.go
@@ -1000,11 +1000,37 @@ func validate(cluster *v1beta1.Cluster, policy *v1beta1.VirtualClusterPolicy) er
 }
 
 // lookupServiceCIDR attempts to determine the cluster's service CIDR.
-// It first attempts to create a failing Service (with an invalid cluster IP)and extracts the expected CIDR from the resulting error.
-// If that fails, it searches the 'kube-apiserver' Pod's arguments for the --service-cluster-ip-range flag.
+// It first reads the default 'kubernetes' ServiceCIDR object (Kubernetes 1.33+).
+// If that fails, it attempts to create a failing Service (with an invalid cluster IP) and extracts the expected CIDR from the resulting error.
+// If that fails too, it searches the 'kube-apiserver' Pod's arguments for the --service-cluster-ip-range flag.
 func (c *Reconciler) lookupServiceCIDR(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
 	log := ctrl.LoggerFrom(ctx)
 
+	// The apiserver publishes its --service-cluster-ip-range as the default ServiceCIDR, named 'kubernetes'.
+	// With the IPAddress allocator (default since 1.33) the failing Service error doesn't report the valid range anymore.
+
+	log.V(1).Info("Looking up Service CIDR from the default ServiceCIDR")
+
+	var defaultServiceCIDR networkingv1.ServiceCIDR
+
+	err := c.Client.Get(ctx, types.NamespacedName{Name: "kubernetes"}, &defaultServiceCIDR)
+	if err != nil {
+		log.V(1).Info("Default ServiceCIDR not available: " + err.Error())
+	}
+
+	if err == nil && len(defaultServiceCIDR.Spec.CIDRs) > 0 {
+		// on dual-stack hosts the first CIDR is the primary IP family
+		serviceCIDR := defaultServiceCIDR.Spec.CIDRs[0]
+		log.V(1).Info("Found Service CIDR from the default ServiceCIDR: " + serviceCIDR)
+
+		_, serviceCIDRAddr, err := net.ParseCIDR(serviceCIDR)
+		if err != nil {
+			return "", err
+		}
+
+		return serviceCIDRAddr.String(), nil
+	}
+
 	// Try to look for the serviceCIDR creating a failing service.
 	// The error should contain the expected serviceCIDR

+func Test_lookupServiceCIDR(t *testing.T) {
+	defaultServiceCIDR := func(cidrs ...string) *networkingv1.ServiceCIDR {
+		return &networkingv1.ServiceCIDR{
+			ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: "kubernetes"},
+			Spec:       networkingv1.ServiceCIDRSpec{CIDRs: cidrs},
+		}
+	}
+
+	apiServerPod := &corev1.Pod{
+		ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{
+			Name:      "kube-apiserver",
+			Namespace: "kube-system",
+			Labels:    map[string]string{"component": "kube-apiserver", "tier": "control-plane"},
+		},
+		Spec: corev1.PodSpec{
+			Containers: []corev1.Container{{
+				Name: "kube-apiserver",
+				Args: []string{"--service-cluster-ip-range=10.96.0.0/12"},
+			}},
+		},
+	}
+
+	tests := []struct {
+		name    string
+		objs    []client.Object
+		want    string
+		wantErr bool
+	}{
+		{
+			name: "from the default ServiceCIDR",
+			objs: []client.Object{defaultServiceCIDR("172.20.0.0/16")},
+			want: "172.20.0.0/16",
+		},
+		{
+			name: "dual-stack ServiceCIDR returns the primary family",
+			objs: []client.Object{defaultServiceCIDR("fd00:10:96::/112", "10.96.0.0/16")},
+			want: "fd00:10:96::/112",
+		},
+		{
+			name: "ServiceCIDR takes precedence over the kube-apiserver pod",
+			objs: []client.Object{defaultServiceCIDR("172.20.0.0/16"), apiServerPod},
+			want: "172.20.0.0/16",
+		},
+		{
+			name: "falls back to the kube-apiserver pod without a ServiceCIDR",
+			objs: []client.Object{apiServerPod},
+			want: "10.96.0.0/12",
+		},
+		{
+			name:    "invalid ServiceCIDR",
+			objs:    []client.Object{defaultServiceCIDR("not-a-cidr")},
+			wantErr: true,
+		},
+		{
+			name: "nothing found",
+			want: "",
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			r := &Reconciler{Client: newTestClient(t, tt.objs...)}
+
+			got, err := r.lookupServiceCIDR(context.Background())
+			if tt.wantErr {
+				require.Error(t, err)
+				return
+			}
+
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			assert.Equal(t, tt.want, got)
+		})
+	}
+}
